Hi, Peter!
Beck talks about the "valley of regret" from an organizational investment angle. I see something else: a fundamental cognitive shift. When a junior works with AI, they are not just compressing search time, they are building their mental models differently. In "Cognitive Divergence Theory " I show this is exactly the kind of early exposure that creates cognitive patterns different from seniors who learned without AI. It is not about productivity, it is about how technical thinking forms in a world where the tool is already intelligent.

Maxim Geraskin I’m not sure I have an answer right now. In general, they’ll need to be able to explain to the LLM how it should work: what the intended behavior is, not what code needs to be written.
I believe that, in the future, system design and architecture for simple projects will be handled by AI. To handle complex, large-scale solutions, juniors will need to become seniors anyway. so it's not a case.
